name: vwap_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index deviates more than 1.5 rolling standard deviations below session VWAP AND RSI(36) simultaneously confirms oversold conditions (RSI < 38), two independent signals of short-term exhaustion align. The VWAP z-score catches the statistical magnitude of dislocation — at z=-1.5 with 10-min rolling std, this is approximately 15-25 spot points below the institutional benchmark price, triggering VWAP-benchmarked algorithms to begin accumulating. The RSI exhaustion filter removes false positives where VWAP is stretched but price momentum is still negative (indicating continued selling pressure), keeping only entries where both the deviation depth AND the velocity of selling have abated. This dual-confirmation is the specific differentiator from v18 (which uses pure deviation momentum without RSI) and v19 (which uses range contraction microstructure): here the RSI acts as a sell-flow exhaustion gate, distinct from either magnitude-based or range-based filtering.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) — reset each session
indicators.purpose: Cumulative from session open — no scaling applies. VWAP is a running statistic, not a windowed lookback. Institutional VWAP benchmarking is the core structural driver of reversion.

indicators.name: close_std_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling std for z-score denominator. Chosen at 120 bars (not 12x original's 60 = 720) because: (1) we need the denominator to reflect CURRENT session volatility regime, (2) 10 min captures enough recent bars to be statistically stable while staying responsive to intraday vol changes. The original's 60-bar 1-min window (=60 min) was too long for our 15-90s hold context.

indicators.name: vwap_zscore
indicators.purpose: Measures deviation from fair value in units of current volatility regime. Threshold -1.5 corresponds to approximately 15-25 NIFTY spot points below VWAP at typical intraday volatility, where VWAP-benchmarked algos start accumulating aggressively.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI on 5-second bars. Scaled from original RSI(14) on 1-min to RSI(36) on 5s: 14 × 1min = 14 min total lookback, which is too slow for our 15-90s hold. RSI(36) = 3 minutes captures recent momentum velocity exhaustion at the timescale of our trade. RSI(14) at 5s would be only 70 seconds — too noisy. This is the primary entry gate: RSI must also be oversold/overbought to confirm sell/buy flow exhaustion before VWAP algorithms step in.

indicators.name: vix_close
indicators.formula: India VIX close, aligned backward to spot bars
indicators.purpose: Regime filter from original. Original uses VIX < 20. In high-VIX environments, VWAP mean reversion fails because sustained institutional directional flows overwhelm the gravitational pull. Kept at same absolute threshold (20) because VIX levels have a structural meaning independent of bar frequency.

buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions on same 5-second bar. No multi-bar confirmation — RSI exhaustion on a 3-min window is sufficient gate.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 points because dual-confirmation entries (VWAP z-score + RSI) target 15-25 NIFTY spot pt deviations; if price moves another 8 spot pts against us (4 option pts at delta 0.5) after both signals fired, the thesis is clearly wrong. Slightly wider than v19 (4 pts) because the RSI gate means we may enter slightly before the absolute bottom of the deviation.
exit.target_rationale: 7 points captures ~50% of the expected reversion from z=-1.5 toward z=0. At 10-min rolling std of ~15-20 NIFTY spot pts, a z=-1.5 deviation is ~22-30 spot pts; reversion from z=-1.5 to z=-0.5 is ~15-20 spot pts = 7-10 option pts at delta 0.5. Targeting 7 pts (50% of typical reversion) gives R:R of 1:1.75.

filters.vix_filter: vix_close < 20.0 — carried from original; high VIX destroys VWAP reversion as institutional flows become directional
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; RSI and rolling std need 120 bars (10 min) warmup before first signal
filters.volume_filter: none — RSI + VWAP z-score combination implicitly filters low-activity bars
filters.trend_filter: none — RSI exhaustion filter implicitly avoids strong trend entries
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-medium — structural VWAP benchmarking is persistent; RSI exhaustion is a stable behavioral pattern at the 3-min timescale

adaptation_notes: Original traded Nifty50 individual stocks at 1-min resolution with RSI(14), volume surge, and ATR-based stops. Key changes: (1) Universe changed from stock basket to NIFTY index — index VWAP is more institutionally anchored; (2) RSI(14) on 1-min compressed to RSI(36) on 5s (3-min equivalent) to match our 15-90s hold time; (3) Rolling std window changed from 60 bars × 1 min (60 min) to 120 bars × 5s (10 min) for current-regime sensitivity; (4) VIX filter kept at VIX < 20 (same threshold, different data source); (5) ATR-based stops replaced with fixed option premium points (4 stop / 7 target) calibrated to NIFTY ATM delta ~0.5; (6) Volume surge indicator dropped — RSI exhaustion is a cleaner filter at 5s frequency than volume ratio; (7) Hold time compressed from 10-60 min to 15-90s.
weaknesses: RSI(36) on 5s bars can still be noisy near session open — warmup filter at 09:20 helps but may not fully prevent early false signals
VIX filter (< 20) reduces opportunity set significantly on high-volatility days that might otherwise have excellent mean reversion
Dual-confirmation requirement (both z-score AND RSI must fire) reduces trade frequency vs v18/v19 — may produce too few trades on range-bound low-vol days
VWAP z-score may fire near day lows/highs that are structural breakouts rather than overshoots — no explicit day-range filter
